Neither debater establishes its number, so I can't pick a winner.

**Debater A (9)** gives an upper bound that is asserted, not exhibited. The per-plane count of 3 crossings is not justified, and the lower-bound step ("fewer crossings would trivialize the tangles") is a conclusion restated as an argument. A's own note concedes this.

**Debater B (7)** also gives an unverified upper bound. The tangle arithmetic (1 + 1 + 5) is not shown to produce a valid tri-plane diagram that satisfies the pairwise-unlink and trivial-tangle conditions. The Farey-graph lower bound is named but never stated, so it cannot exclude 6 or fewer crossings. B also calls the extra crossings "surplus" without showing they are unnecessary.

Both sides therefore lack a verified diagram or a verified obstruction. I also can't confirm the value from the published literature on bridge trisections of spun knots, so I can't say whether the true tri-plane crossing number is 7, 9, or something else. A correct resolution needs an explicit minimal tri-plane diagram together with a rigorous lower bound.

DECISION: NEITHER
